money_at_stake.rationale: TMC's own Subpart-1300-compliant technical economic assessments put combined project value (NPV) at $23.6 billion across the NORI-D Pre-Feasibility Study ($5.5B NPV) and the Initial Assessment covering the remaining NORI and TOML areas ($18.1B NPV), the same figure the occurrence's Q2 2026 corporate update and March 2026 investor materials both still carry as current project economics. $23.6B sits inside the $10-100B band with room on both sides. This is the pool the whole nodule-to-refined-metal chain moves, of which the Brownsville landside refining park (this card's specific retail gap) captures the processing/refining leg; no separate dollar figure for the Brownsville facility alone has been published as of this appraisal, so the wider project NPV is used as the sized pool rather than an unsourced facility-specific estimate.

public_reach.rationale: The $23.6B project-economics pool sits primarily on TMC the metals company Inc. (Nasdaq: TMC), the listed issuer that holds the NOAA exploration and commercial-recovery rights and whose own filings state the NPV figure. Held at 70 rather than 85+ because the specific retail-gap layer this card exists to flag, the Brownsville landside refining park, is being co-developed with Mariana Minerals, which this run's search found described only as a privately founded engineering/metallurgical-processing partner (ex-Tesla/Exxon/BASF team) with no public listing found; the port-development, EPC and permitting-services contractors behind the park are, per the signal card's own retail_gap text, not named by any source found this run, so an unknown share of the landside buildout's own capital may land on private engineering and construction firms rather than TMC directly. The offshore mining and reserve-holding side (the larger share of the $23.6B) is unambiguously on the listed entity; the landside processing side (the specific gap) is mixed with a real private component.

capture_odds.rationale: The economics TMC itself discloses show real margin capture rather than a commodity pass-through: steady-state EBITDA margin of 43% for the NORI-D Project and approximately 57% for the combined Initial Assessment areas, against C1 cash costs of $1,065 per tonne of nickel including byproduct credits. That is a wide, qualification-and-permit-gated margin, not a price-taker return, and it is reinforced by the PFS marking what TMC calls a world-first declaration of Probable Mineral Reserves for deep-sea polymetallic nodules, i.e. a first-mover regulatory position with no operating precedent to compete against yet. Held at 65 rather than higher because two things cap confidence: these are the company's own pre-production technical-report projections, not realized operating margins, and the final output (nickel, cobalt, copper, manganese) still sells into commodity metal markets whose prices are outside TMC's control regardless of how efficiently it mines and refines.

timing_fit.rationale: Money is moving inside the window on two fronts at once: the Brownsville MSA (2026-07-21, this appraisal's anchor) has already started mobilization, concept development and technical design work toward plant feasibility, self-fetched and confirmed this run; and TMC's own NORI-D economics target production ramp-up to 12 million tonnes per annum of wet nodules within the first five years of operation, squarely inside the 2-5 year horizon. Held at 72 rather than higher because two real gates sit ahead of committed capital: NOAA's first-ever consolidated exploration-and-commercial-recovery permit review (Federal Register publication 2026-08-19, comment period running into October 2026) has no committed decision date, and the Brownsville park itself is only at concept design and feasibility, not a sanctioned final investment decision. The money is credibly inside the window rather than merely projected past it, but a first-of-its-kind US federal permit process is exactly the kind of catalyst that can slip.
